  1. com.sbancuz.offscreen.api

Troubleshooting and limits

Start with the symptom below. Check the call or file that produced the result, inspect its reported failure and apply the matching correction before retrying.

Installation checklist

  • Minecraft 1.12.2, Java 25, and Cleanroom with its SDL/LWJGLY backend are required. The declared minimum is Cleanroom 0.7.13-alpha.
  • Place the production OffscreenCleanroom-1.12.2-0.1.1.jar in mods/. Sources, Javadoc, and -mcp archives are not normal game downloads.
  • ModularUI 3.1.6 and Had Enough Items (HEI) 4.36.1 are optional, used only for their respective integrations.
  • For synchronized screens, both sides need OffscreenCleanroom, ModularUI, and the addon registering the factory.

Normal Forge's LWJGL2 backend is unsupported. The library does not automatically detach every screen or add gameplay content. Another mod calls its API to open a window.

No window appears

Call the API on Minecraft's main client thread after initialization. If the call returns null, check which opening method you used:

  • OffscreenAPI.open: the screen supplier returned null, or no adapter was created. For an unsupported screen type, register its adapter in UIRegistry.
  • openOffscreen(): a world or player is missing, a different factory is still opening, or session setup failed. A failed initial request is recorded in the client log.

Screen-supplier and adapter-factory exceptions propagate from OffscreenAPI.open. SDL initialization, native-window, and shared-context creation failures throw IllegalStateException. These failures do not become null results; inspect the exception and the first related error in the game log.

If isOpen(window) returns true but no window is visible, check the client log for [Offscreen] SDL_ShowWindow failed and inspect the SDL error that follows it. The native window was created, but SDL could not show it. isOpen checks the native handle's lifetime; it does not confirm that the window is visible on your desktop.

A window opens without the HEI overlay

Check that HEI is loaded in the client. The built-in adapters add HEI support to container and recipe screens; an ordinary GuiScreen does not receive an overlay. For ModularUI panels, also check whether the panel's recipe-viewer settings disable it. See HEI overlays for supported versions and behavior.

A synchronized window is waiting or failed

The desktop window opens before its synchronized screen is ready. When opened from another hosted screen, it keeps that screen frozen with an animated spinner in the top-right corner until a matching reply arrives. Frozen controls cannot be used. Without a previous screen, the spinner appears on a plain background. OffscreenAPI.isOpen(window) checks the native window; OffscreenAPI.isReady(window) requires successful layout and a healthy synchronized binding.

After 200 client maintenance ticks without a usable reply (about ten seconds during normal ticking), the failed server session is released and a local error screen stays open. Tick-based waits take longer when the client stalls. The timeout means no usable response arrived; it does not prove the server rejected the request.

Choose Retry to send a fresh request in the same desktop window, or Close to dismiss it. Retry is disabled while another synchronized request is pending. Check that the same factory is registered on both sides and that the required addon versions match. Request-send and screen-initialization failures have separate messages; the client/server logs provide technical details when those checks do not resolve the issue.

Use Tab/Shift-Tab to select a button, Enter/Space to activate it, Escape to close, and Up/Down to scroll long messages in a small window. The loading and error screens do not pause the integrated server. Leaving the world closes them.

OffscreenAPI.getStatus(window) returns a detached snapshot: WAITING_FOR_SERVER, INITIALIZING, READY, FAILED or CLOSED. A failed handle keeps its failure reason/message after closure. A null handle is simply closed without a failure. See readiness examples in all five languages and factory setup.

A window redraws slowly

Background windows default to 10 FPS and focused windows to 60 FPS. The limits apply to drawing. Screens still update on client ticks, and the server tick rate is unchanged.

To change them in the config file, close the game and open config/offscreencleanroom.cfg. In its general section, edit I:unfocusedFps=10 or I:focusedFps=60, then restart the game to load the changes. Either setting accepts 0 for unlimited drawing or any integer from 1 to 2,147,483,647 for an FPS cap, such as I:focusedFps=360 or I:focusedFps=813. Actual FPS depends on Minecraft's render loop and hardware; a higher cap does not guarantee that drawing rate.

Drawing or input coordinates do not line up

For custom adapters, use the GUI dimensions supplied to onResize for layout and hit testing.

SDL window size, drawable pixel size, and Minecraft GUI size can differ. GUI callbacks use scaled top-down GUI coordinates; framebuffer readback uses pixel coordinates. Let the adapter handle that conversion instead of multiplying by a guessed scale.

Keys work, but typed text is missing

In a custom HostUI adapter, handle decoded text in onTextInput. Physical key events carry key codes for shortcuts and navigation; their character is normally zero. Do not reconstruct typed text from those codes. The text callback can receive several characters at once, and its default implementation does nothing.

If no text arrives, check the client log for [Offscreen] SDL_StartTextInput failed and inspect the SDL error that follows it. This warning means SDL could not start native text input for the window.

An inventory window closes immediately

The log message Inventories are not supported in a separate window means a GuiInventory was supplied as the window's root screen. That window is closed. For server-owned inventory interactions, use a synchronized factory; Minecraft still allows one active slot container per player.

Navigation and temporary input state

Navigation cannot pop the root screen. A child can return to its parent without disposing the parent.

If a requested screen change does not happen, look for [Offscreen] scoped action failed and inspect its stack trace. The host skips navigation handling for that failed action. [Offscreen] screen-change handling failed instead means the action returned, but processing its screen change failed; inspect that trace for adapter creation or cleanup errors.

The host temporarily installs the screen/input state needed by a callback, then restores the previous state. Do not retain that temporary state in a background thread. A custom adapter's scope() must return a retained scope instance so restoration can use the state saved on entry. The host pairs entry and restoration; the adapter releases its owned resources when disposed.

Calls used in the examples

When you finish: If an open fails, inspect the exception or retained status before retrying. Close only your own window handles and cancel work belonging to the closed screen. A visible waiting screen does not mean a synchronized panel is ready.
